newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates were quoted lower in Zimbabwe's money market which opened liquid on Wednesday, dealers said.

They said the central Reserve Bank auctioned Z$580 million of 30-day treasury bills, breaking from the usual 91-day paper it offers to discount houses. On Wednesday, the central bank sold the bills at 17.36 percent, down from 17.50 percent the previous day.
Meanwhile, treasury bills were being sold on the secondary market at 17 percent from 17.40 while call money, also trading at 17 percent, was half a percentage point easier.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were quoted at 18.25 and 17.50 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 18.75 and 17.85 percent while bankers acceptances were quoted stable at 18 percent (buying) but softer at 17 percent from 17.50 percent (selling).
Figures from the central bank indicated the market closed with a surplus of Z$141 million on Tuesday, up from Monday's Z$101.2 million.
